record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Asymptotic Geometric Analysis
record.context_brief: simplex conjecture for random simplex volume
record.original_question: For an n-dimensional convex body K, let m_1(K) be the expected normalized volume of the random simplex conv{x_1, ..., x_{n+1}} generated by n+1 independent uniformly distributed points in K. Is it true that m_1(K) <= m_1(S_n) for every convex body K in R^n, where S_n is any n-dimensional simplex?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be an $n$-dimensional convex body (a compact convex set with nonempty interior) of positive volume. Let $x_1, \dots, x_{n+1}$ be independent random points distributed uniformly in $K$, and define the normalized expected volume of the random simplex
$$ m_1(K) \;=\; \frac{\mathbb{E}\,\mathrm{vol}_n\!\big(\operatorname{conv}\{x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}\}\big)}{\mathrm{vol}_n(K)}. $$
Let $S_n \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ denote any $n$-dimensional simplex (the value $m_1(S_n)$ is independent of the choice of simplex by affine invariance). Prove or disprove: for every $n \ge 2$ and every $n$-dimensional convex body $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$,
$$ m_1(K) \;\le\; m_1(S_n). $$
Equivalently, among all $n$-dimensional convex bodies, the normalized expected volume of the random simplex spanned by $n+1$ uniform points is maximized by simplices.
artifact.status_search_result: The simplex conjecture (random simplex volume is maximized by simplices) is classically known to hold in dimension 2 (Blaschke's solution of Sylvester's problem) and in dimension 3 (the tetrahedron case, established by Reed/Buchta-Reitzner). It remains an open conjecture in general dimension $n \ge 4$.

status_evidence.title: On the monotonicity of the expected volume of a random simplex
status_evidence.snippet: Monotonicity of expected volume of a random simplex holds for d=1,2, fails for d≥4; relates to slicing conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Connected problem on random simplex volumes; results known only in low dimensions.

status_evidence.title: The convex hull of random points in a tetrahedron: Solution of Blaschke's problem and more general results
status_evidence.snippet: Solution of Blaschke's problem in the tetrahedron case.
status_evidence.claim: The 3-dimensional case (tetrahedron) of the simplex conjecture has been resolved.
